about.labels: correctId is a TheMovieDB movie id as a number. "none" means no entry for this film exists, or the listing is not one identifiable film. "unclear" means a human could not settle it either - exclude those rows from scoring rather than counting them against anything.
about.noCandidates: Candidate lists are deliberately NOT stored. TheMovieDB reorders search results by a popularity score it recomputes daily, and adds, merges and deletes entries continuously, so a frozen copy of a result list stops describing anything real within days. Scoring re-runs the search.
about.notABenchmark: Do NOT read an accuracy figure off the whole file. Every row here was selected because it was already known to be hard, so the population is the tail and not a sample of listings. What it measures is whether a change helps on the cases that were going wrong, which is the question worth asking - it is not an estimate of how often the pipeline is right.

samples.unmatched: Listings categorised as a film that no release matched at all. The other half of the failure surface: these cost a missed match rather than a wrong one.
samples.unstable: Listings whose published match changed between releases, found by helpers/find-unstable-matches.js. At least one of the published answers was wrong, which is what makes them worth labelling without anyone having flagged them.

about.selfContained: Rows embed their own input text on purpose. The listings themselves fall out of retrieved-data and transformed-data within weeks, and showingId is kept only for provenance - nothing here needs those releases to still exist.
about.twoFailures: Because the search is re-run, a wrong answer has two possible causes and they are not the same problem. Either the search never returned the right film, which no matcher can fix, or it did and the matcher chose wrong. A harness that does not separate these will blame the matcher for the search. Check whether correctId appears in the candidate list before scoring the choice.
about.what: Hand-adjudicated TheMovieDB matches for real cinema listings. Each row carries the input a matcher sees - title, year, runtime, classification, billed cast and crew, and the listing description - alongside the TheMovieDB id a human judged correct. Built while evaluating TypeSafe Jev against the incumbent LLM at the review-the-search-results step in September 2026, but it is not specific to either: it scores anything that maps a listing to a TheMovieDB id.

rows.description:
Best Bulgarian Feature Documentary – Rhodope International Documentary Film Festival, 2025
Best Sound in a Documentary – Vasil Gendov Awards, Union of Bulgarian Filmmakers, 2025
Soul Beyond Measure is an award-winning feature documentary about people from different nationalities who have turned their fascination with Bulgarian and Balkan folklore into a passion and a way of life.
With no ancestral connection to Bulgaria or the Balkans, they have dedicated years to learning and sharing Bulgarian folk dances, songs and traditional music in their own countries. The film asks what has drawn people from some of the world‘s wealthiest nations to Bulgaria since the days of the Iron Curtain - to learn its dances, collect songs from elderly village singers, master traditional instruments and wear Bulgarian folk costumes with extraordinary pride and joy.
Filmed over nearly seven years across Bulgaria, Belgium, Germany, Switzerland, the United States and Japan, Soul Beyond Measure is ultimately about much more than folklore. Through deeply personal stories, it explores love, belonging, identity, friendship, loss and the remarkable ability of music and dance to connect people across cultures and borders.
rows.title: Soul Beyond Measure

rows.description:
Local film critic and podcaster Matthew Turner returns for a third mini season of film noir classics, which will run exclusively at Chiswick Cinema throughout November 2026.

"Former crooner Dick Powell stars as hard-boiled private eye Philip Marlowe, who's drawn into a web of crime and corruption when he's hired to locate Velma (Claire Trevor), the former girlfriend of hulking ex-con Moose Malloy (Mike Mazurki). Adapted from the classic detective novel by Raymond Chandler and released the same year as Double Indemnity, this is considered one of the pinnacles of film noir and a key influence on the genre."

Synopsis:
After being hired to find an ex-con's former girlfriend, Philip Marlowe is drawn into a deeply complex web of mystery and deceit.
rows.title: Farewell, My Lovely [a.k.a Murder, My Sweet]

rows.description:
Released in the cinema as part of Maggie’s Cancer Centre 30th Anniversary celebrations. We're delighted to welcome the film's director and other special guests for a Q&A after the film. Filmed partly at Maggie's West London, Charing Cross Hospital. Most box office revenue will go to this important local charity. 
Nearly one in two of us will be diagnosed with cancer at some point in our lives. David Nicholas Wilkinson is one of them, twice over. In 2020, a colonoscopy found his bowel to be extremely healthy for a man his age. In 2023, a FIT test came back clear and, like almost everyone who takes one, he assumed that meant the all-clear. In 2024, a second colonoscopy found bowel cancer. Stage 4. He was told his tumour was 5-6 years old. What went wrong? A FIT test looks for blood. Wilkinson’s tumour never bled. Nor do a great many others.
1 IN 2 follows Wilkinson through his own treatment, where he discovers a steep rise in bowel cancer among people far too young to be screened for it, and far too young, it seems, to be believed. Among those who tell him their stories is a bowel surgeon whose own symptoms were dismissed by her oncologist colleagues and in part by herself because she was only 44.
Bowel cancer is very insidious; it often strikes with few or no symptoms. One of the participants, an NHS nurse specialising in colonoscopies, had only one symptom: anxiety. 1 IN 2 attempts to flag up early signs because the one thing no one wants is to end up like director David Nicholas Wilkinson, with stage 4 bowel cancer.
rows.title: 1 in 2

rows.description:
Richard Linklater’s film restages the unconventional filming of Jean-Luc Godard’s influential feature debut Breathless, a stylish crime drama about a petty thief turned cop killer pursuing an American girl in 1960s Paris. The film seamlessly recreates one of cinema's most ground breaking productions and at the same time pays tribute to its accomplishment with infectious admiration.

“Richard Linklater’s Nouvelle Vague is a beautiful, admiring portrait of a turning point in cinema.” Wendy Ide, The Observer

“Richard Linklater’s love letter to an iconic era of French cinema, this portrayal of the creation of Breathless, Jean-Luc Godard’s first feature film, celebrates Frenchness at its most proudly awkward.” Donald Clarke, Irish Times
rows.title: Nouvelle Vague

rows.description:
My Cinema Clinic: Menopause is an exciting new cinema brand, bringing a specially made thought-provoking documentary alongside an expert panel to a cinema location near you.

The Menopause event will include a 60-minute myth busting cinematic documentary, directed by BAFTA award-winning director Lily Murray to provide the very latest scientific and holistic viewpoints on the perimenopause and post-menopause.
The film features some central figures from the menopause movement in the UK including Kate Muir, Dr Nighat Arif and Diane Danzebrink.

Shot with stunning cinematography of nature, the film takes us through the perimenopause and post-menopause journeys of a wide spectrum of women punctuated by medical and holistic insights. It offers potential remedies and explains why support is needed and where it is available. It bares witness to what the experience feels like on the other side of this often challenging transition period.

After the 60-minute film, a panel of local menopause GP, experts and advocates will serve as a pop-up menopause clinic at each cinema and will be available to those who wish to share their stories, asks questions and discuss what would best support them in their own journeys.
rows.title: My Cinema Clinic: Menopause

rows.description:
At a garden party on a sunny afternoon, Alice is surprised to see her parents? friend Lewis Carroll transform into a white rabbit. When she follows him down a rabbit hole, events become curiouser and curiouser?As Alice journeys through Wonderland, she encounters countless strange creatures. She?s swept off her feet by the charming Knave of Hearts, who?s on the run for stealing the tarts. Confusion piles upon confusion. Then Alice wakes with a start. Was it all a daydream? 
Christopher Wheeldon?s Alice?s Adventures in Wonderland burst onto the stage in 2011 in an explosion of colour, stage magic and inventive, sophisticated choreography. Joby Talbot?s score combines contemporary soundworlds with sweeping melodies that gesture to ballet scores of the 19th century. Bob Crowley?s wildly imaginative, eye-popping designs draw on everything from puppetry to projections to make Wonderland wonderfully real. The result shows The Royal Ballet at its best, bringing together world-class dance with enchanting family entertainment and ingenious music and design.
rows.title: Alices Adventures In Wonderland - LIVE - The Royal Ballet 26-27

rows.description:
Revisit the changing face of British culture through a series of iconic films which defined the 90s

Orlando lives for 400 years. His story begins in the court of Elizabeth I, where he is a young man in search of love and freedom. Centuries later, he continues the journey as a woman.

Tilda Swinton leads the cast in Sally Potter’s bold and beautiful film, based on the novel by Virginia Woolf. Witty, romantic and full of striking images, Orlando is a story about identity, desire and the freedom to become who you are.
rows.title: The 90s on Screen: Orlando

Duration: 180

Special screening of Babylon. Free entry with an Eventbrite ticket only. Download yours before attending.

Join us for a special screening of Babylon as part of the Hidden Beach Summer of Culture.

Directed by Franco Rosso, Babylon is a landmark British drama that captures the energy, creativity, and challenges of London's reggae sound system culture at the dawn of the 1980s. Starring Brinsley Forde, the film follows Blue, a talented young DJ whose passion for music is tested as he confronts racism, discrimination, and the pressures of everyday life while preparing his sound system for a major clash.

Driven by an iconic reggae soundtrack and an authentic portrayal of Black British life, the film explores themes of identity, resilience, community, and the power of music as a form of expression and resistance. Widely regarded as one of the defining works of Black British cinema, Babylon remains as powerful and relevant today as when it was first released.

Following the screening, guests are invited to stay for an informal Film + Conversation session, offering the opportunity to reflect on the film's themes, share perspectives, and explore its lasting cultural significance.

This event forms part of Hidden Beach's Film + Conversation Night series, celebrating films that inspire conversation, creativity, and cultural understanding.

Free admission. Entry is by advance Eventbrite ticket only. Every attendee must have a free Eventbrite ticket to gain entry. Spaces are limited, so please book early to avoid disappointment.
rows.title: Babylon - Film Screening at Bojangles
